Once upon a time, there was a little fox named Pip. Pip lived near a river with his mother. Every morning, Pip ran to the water and looked at the fish. "I want to catch one," he said. His mother smiled and said, "Be patient, Pip."

One day, a small bird came to the river. The bird was sad because she had lost her nest. Pip wanted to help. "Let us find a new home for you," said Pip. They looked in the trees and under the bushes. At last they found a warm hole in an old tree. The bird was very happy and sang a song for Pip.

Tom had a red ball. He liked to play with it in the park every day. One sunny afternoon, the ball rolled down the hill and into the pond. Tom was sad. A kind girl named Mia saw the ball floating on the water. She found a long stick and pulled the ball back to the shore. "Thank you!" said Tom. "Do you want to play with me?" Mia said yes, and they played until the sun went down.

Lily was a little girl who loved to draw. She drew cats, dogs, trees and the big yellow sun. One rainy day, she could not go outside, so she drew a picture of a rainbow. Her dad saw the picture and said, "That is so pretty! Let us put it on the wall." Lily felt proud. From that day on, she drew a new picture every morning.

There was a big, old bear who lived in a cave. He was lonely because he had no friends. A little rabbit came by and said, "Hello, Mr. Bear. Why do you look so sad?" The bear told the rabbit that nobody wanted to talk to him. The rabbit laughed and said, "I will be your friend." From then on, the bear and the rabbit played together every day, and the bear was never lonely again.
